title: Company-level objective threading with milestone runway and stakeholder commitment ledger
creator: Marina Chen
description: Summary: create a lightweight, auditable process to thread company-level OKRs into deliverable milestones across product, engineering, design, and ops. Deliver a ‘milestone runway’ (quarter-to-quarter milestone map) plus a simple 'commitment ledger' that captures explicit stakeholder commitments, acceptance criteria, and rollback gates for each initiative. Purpose: reduce ambiguity during cross-team planning, make trade-offs visible at quarterly planning, and create a single source of truth for exec decisioning on scope/deferrals.
context_and_problem: Current issues observed during Q1 planning: (1) teams land on conflicting milestone assumptions (dates vs. capacity), (2) OKR ownership is high-level and not mapped to concrete release milestones, (3) executive decisions to defer features happen late with incomplete visibility into downstream work. This ticket scopes a PM-led pattern to solve those gaps and integrate with the roadmap cadence and release gating.
outcome_and_success_metrics: All company-level OKRs have at least one mapped milestone per quarter by planning freeze (target 100%)
Reduction in post-planning scope deferrals by 40% compared to last quarter
>90% stakeholder sign-off rate on commitment ledger entries before quarter kickoff
Dashboard shows initiative-level milestone completion and early warning flags for 80% of initiatives
acceptance_criteria: Milestone runway template published to Confluence with examples for three initiatives
Commitment ledger prototype (spreadsheet + Confluence template) used by 6 pilot teams during planning cycle
Roadmap dashboard updated to ingest milestone metadata and surface 'at-risk' status
Stakeholder review session complete with recorded decisions and updated ledger entries
decisions: Use a single-sourced milestone ID per initiative to link roadmap, console rollout, and release notes; avoids duplicate tracking
Adopt a lightweight signoff mechanism (PM + Eng lead + Design lead) instead of formal RACI for speed
Rollbacks will be defined as explicit gates on the ledger; each gate includes success metrics and fallback plan
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tradeoff: adding ledger signoff increases planning overhead vs. clarity gained — mitigated by a concise template and 30-minute signoff meetings
Risk: engineering capacity estimates may be inaccurate early in the cycle — mitigate via two-stage estimates (rough, then firm) and buffer allocation
Risk: executives may request scope changes after signoff; require documented re-evaluation using ledger impact matrix
